workflow: Host-native image generation followed by sprite extraction; no third-party sheet repackaging
sourcePrompt: Create a premium illustrated top-down fantasy tabletop map ASSET ATLAS for a weathered coastal harbor town. Exactly 12 separate objects in a precise invisible 4-column by 3-row equal-cell layout, landscape 1536 by 1024 canvas. Transparent background throughout, no ground, no text, no labels, no grid lines, no border. Each object centered in its own equal cell, with generous TRANSPARENT GUTTER of at least 15 percent on all sides, no overlap or touching adjacent objects. True overhead orthographic 90-degree view, NOT isometric or perspective. Cohesive hand-painted cartographic realism: tactile wooden grain, individually detailed slate/shingle/tile textures, patinated metals, moss at joints, subtle wear, crisp readable silhouette, muted sea-green/ochre/brown/slate palette, light from upper left. Extremely restrained short contact shadows entirely inside each cell; no huge long shadows or ambient ground. Objects occupy 65-72% of their cell width/height. Row1 left to right: 1 a small rectangular cottage slate roof seen strictly from directly above, roof ridge horizontal, stone chimney and patched shingles; 2 a longer rectangular timber harbor warehouse roof, terracotta/weathered cedar shingles, horizontal ridge and tiny roof vents; 3 a square market stall striped faded ochre and sea-green canvas canopy, rough timber counter with baskets around its edges; 4 a circular old stone well seen directly from above with dark central opening, timber crossbeam and bucket. Row2 left to right: 5 a wooden two-wheel handcart loaded with sacks, strict overhead; 6 a small cluster of two weathered wood crates and a rope-bound barrel, strict overhead; 7 a luxuriant broadleaf oak canopy with individually painted foliage clumps, irregular circular silhouette, no visible tree trunk from side; 8 an evergreen pine canopy seen directly from above, irregular star-shaped foliage tiers, no side elevation. Row3 left to right: 9 a low shrub cluster with green leaves and tiny cream flowers, overhead; 10 a timber single bed with teal blanket, cream pillow, folded ochre quilt at foot, top down; 11 a round oak table with plates, loaf, unmarked parchment and one stool, top down; 12 a wide open timber doorway threshold module viewed overhead, two short stone jamb blocks and open wooden door leaf attached at one jamb swinging inward, no surrounding wall. This is production sprite artwork, clean alpha silhouette and fine detail. Do not draw scenery, a room, a backdrop, a collage frame, or a character.
correctionPrompt: Edit this asset atlas, preserving the cohesive harbor-town painting style and the 11 successful objects. Production corrections: (1) Make all 12 sprites fit completely inside a precise invisible 4-column x 3-row layout, each with at least 35 pixels of absolutely transparent gutter on all sides. Especially shrink the round table/stool slightly and move it right so no part crosses into the bed cell at x=768. Keep the canvas 1536x1024. (2) Replace the bottom-right doorway, which is incorrectly front/side elevation, with a STRICTLY VERTICAL OVERHEAD doorway module: two small square stone jamb blocks at left and right, a horizontal threshold between them, a thin open door LEAF seen edge-on as a narrow wood plank swinging diagonally upward into the cell from the left jamb. No visible upright lintel, no facade, no arch. It must be the same true bird's-eye view as a floor plan. (3) Ensure objects have fully opaque painted interiors with smooth alpha edges. Background and all gutters MUST be fully alpha-zero transparent. No colored atmosphere or ground. No new text, no grid or borders. Retain fine roof tiles, timber grain, soft foliage and muted teal ochre slate colors. Light from top-left, only very short contact shadows within each sprite. Do not remove details or simplify.
review: First sheet supplies 11 objects; perspective doorway excluded. Correction fixes doorway perspective but fails alpha inspection; no bytes from it enter HTML.
